why: The statement is a universal claim over all transcendental entire functions; the Martí-Pete–Rempe–Waterman paper exhibits one with a bounded (singleton) component of I(f), which refutes it as worded, so scope whole, direction refuted, object a counterexample, verified by JAMS acceptance. Its first public written argument is the 23 Aug 2021 arXiv v1 (the paper's title already names Eremenko's conjecture; later versions are revisions of the same argument), so it predates the snapshot. Pre-snapshot partials (Rippon-Stallard 2005, Rempe 2007, Rippon-Stallard 2011, Nicks-Rippon-Stallard 2018) are cases. RRRS and Brown address the strong curve form, and Rempe-Gillen addresses Julia continua: variants. Rempe-Gillen's 2026 v5 is a revision of a 2016 paper, and the record does not show new mathematics on this question, so it stays dated 2016. The close call is the 2026 expository note by the same authors. It gives a more direct proof of a result already established, so it does not move the problem. I scored it none as exposition of a known result rather than a new whole. Its AI disclosure (Copilot and Claude Opus 5 for drafting, copy-editing and a figure; 'AI tools did not supply new mathematical arguments') is none, and ai.systems is empty.
doubts: The 2021 date assumes v1 already contained the counterexample (the v1 PDF was unreadable). If the construction first appeared in v5 (30 Oct 2024), the event would move after the snapshot and still be whole/digested/refuted. Scoring the 2026 note as none rather than whole is a judgement: it re-proves the singleton case by a different route but adds nothing to the problem's status.
